skill.name: extension-oql
skill.description: Make a canister's data queryable by the Caffeine Data Intelligence agent. Use whenever an app stores structured data (Maps/Lists/arrays of records) that should be answerable in natural language — "top customers", "revenue by region", "active projects". Adds a discoverable `schema()` and a JSON `execute()` query endpoint via the `caffeineai-oql` mops package's `Expose` mixin.
skill.summary: Expose structured Motoko canister data through OQL with schema discovery, relationships, and per-entity authorization.
skill.author: caffeinelabs

security_audit.summary: All 115 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, Motoko examples, a fixed Mops setup command, the `keys()` method, and sample records. SKILL.md contains no shell backtick execution, key-file access, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or data-exfiltration intent. It documents explicit per-entity authorization and warns developers to choose access levels carefully.

and `execute()` both run the check against the live `caller`. No app-wide config,

content.value_statement: Structured canister data is difficult for intelligence agents to query safely. This skill adds OQL entities, schema discovery, query execution, relationships, and per-entity authorization.
actual_capabilities: Integrates the caffeineai-oql Expose mixin to add schema discovery and query execution endpoints.
Maps Motoko Maps, Sets, Lists, and arrays into queryable OQL entities.
Configures public, controller-only, user-scoped, and controller-or-scoped authorization per entity.
Defines foreign-key edges, hidden fields, samples, computed payloads, and flattened records.
Handles nested, optional, variant, collection, and computed data through manual entities or conversion modules.
limitations: Requires caffeineai-oql version 0.4 and Motoko compiler version 1.11 or newer.
Automatic derivation needs flat primitive records unless conversion modules are provided.
The skill does not deploy the canister or validate production data policies.
Incorrect authorization choices can expose more rows than intended.

use_cases.title: Add Canister Analytics
use_cases.description: Expose product, customer, or project collections for natural-language questions and aggregate analysis.

use_cases.title: Protect User-Scoped Queries
use_cases.description: Apply owner fields and scoped authorization so signed-in users receive only permitted rows.

use_cases.title: Model Complex Relationships
use_cases.description: Create edges, junction entities, flattened records, and computed payloads for richer queries.

prompt_templates.title: Expose One Collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my Motoko canister and expose the products collection through caffeineai-oql. Keep controller-only authorization and summarize each change.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with one flat record collection.

prompt_templates.title: Add User Scoping
prompt_templates.prompt: Expose my notes collection. Use its owner principal for row-level access, and prevent users from reading another user's rows.

prompt_templates.title: Connect Related Entities
prompt_templates.prompt: Expose products, vendors, and supplies as related OQL entities. Define stable primary keys and edges that support dotted-path queries.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Complex OQL Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Review all persistent collections. Propose authorized entities, manual projections, conversion modules, hidden fields, samples, and synthetic junctions before implementing them.

output_examples.input: Expose a products map while keeping access limited to controllers.
output: Added a product entity with its identifier as the primary key.
Kept controller-only authorization and added an empty-state schema sample.
Registered schema discovery and query execution through the Expose mixin.

output_examples.input: Make private notes queryable by each note owner.
output: Tagged the owner principal as the row owner.
Applied user-scoped authorization so each caller receives only owned notes.
Kept ownership available during joins to prevent cross-user traversal.

output_examples.input: Connect products and vendors through a supplies collection.
output: Created a manual supply entity from map entries.
Promoted product and vendor identifiers into queryable fields.
Linked both identifiers to their target entities for relationship traversal.

best_practices: Keep controller-only authorization until the intended audience for every entity is explicit.
Expose only fields and collections required for supported questions.
Verify primary keys, owner fields, edges, and empty-collection samples before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not mark private or user-owned data as public.
Do not enable scoped access without a valid owner field or subject-aware iterator.
Do not rely on populated collections for schema discovery when data can be empty.

faq.question: What does this skill add?
faq.answer: It adds queryable OQL entities plus schema discovery and query execution endpoints to a Motoko canister.

faq.question: Which collection types are supported?
faq.answer: Maps, Sets, Lists, immutable arrays, and mutable arrays can use automatic entity conversion for supported row types.

faq.question: How is access controlled?
faq.answer: Each entity selects public, controller-only, user-scoped, or controller-or-scoped authorization.

faq.question: Does it expose every collection automatically?
faq.answer: No. Developers choose which persistent collections become entities and which fields remain visible.

faq.question: What versions are required?
faq.answer: The documented integration uses caffeineai-oql 0.4.0 and requires Motoko compiler 1.11 or newer.

faq.question: How are non-primitive fields handled?
faq.answer: Use manual payloads, flattened records, or type-specific conversion modules that produce one stable OQL value variant.
